fr.elements: Main Building; Secondary Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Internal Drive Aisle; Landscaped Area; Access Road; Street Frontage; Walkway; Utility Area; Dumpster Enclosure
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark each access point with visible signage identifying which building or area it serves.
• Mark the secondary building with its own address or unit identifier visible from the access road.
• Keep the internal drive aisle clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach both structures.
• Post signage at the main access road entry indicating the layout of both buildings for arriving responders.
• Mark a designated staging area for emergency vehicles that does not block the internal drive aisle.
• Keep the area around the dumpster enclosure clear to prevent it from blocking vehicle movement near building access points.
• Trim vegetation along the internal drive aisle to maintain overhead and side clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Mark any rear access points with reflective signage to help responders locate them under limited visibility conditions.
• Keep the utility area clearly marked and accessible so responders can locate shutoffs without searching.
• Keep walkways between the two buildings clear to allow responder foot movement between structures.

wildfire.conditions: Large Paved Area; Open Paved Area; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Limited Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes; Building Cluster
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster to reduce the concentration of vegetation near the building cluster.
• Remove any dead branches or dry plant material from trees located closest to the buildings.
• Keep the open paved areas clear of debris, dry leaves, and plant material that may accumulate near buildings.
• Maintain separation between scattered trees and building walls by trimming branches that extend toward or over rooflines.
• Keep all access routes and drive lanes clear of vegetation encroachment to maintain unobstructed entry and exit for emergency vehicles.
